action: No action needed; for awareness. Staff at sensitive firms should report unusual surveillance, such as strangers photographing screens or unfamiliar network devices in public places.
date_note: Date of The Record's report; the charges were filed this week.
exec: Foreign agents are alleged to be physically watching staff at a major data and defence software firm, so in-person security matters too.
plain: US authorities charged a Russian man with acting as a Russian agent and watching Palantir employees, including photographing their laptop screens in cafés.

key_findings: The Record reports a Russian national, Igor Andreevich D'iu, was charged in the US this week.
Charges reported: conspiring to act as an agent of Russia, acting as a foreign agent without notifying the attorney general, interstate stalking and identity document fraud.
Alleged conduct: photographing employees' laptop screens at Palo Alto cafés and planting Wi-Fi equipment.
He is alleged to have been recruited via Telegram and paid three times at $15,000.

sources.name: The Record: Russian charged with spying on Palantir employees for Moscow

summary: The Record reports that US authorities charged Russian national Igor Andreevich D'iu with acting as an agent of Russia and related offences. He is alleged to have photographed Palantir employees' laptop screens in Palo Alto cafés and planted Wi-Fi equipment. The charges are allegations; the DOJ original was not read.
title: Russian man charged with spying on Palantir employees for Moscow

validation.note: The Record article read; DOJ release not read.
